texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 09.04.2019 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. Brief facts of the case as per charge sheet is that, on 30.11.2018, the injured Amod Kumar Shah S/o Sh. Suranjan Shah was coming from his duty from Cannaught Place. He set down on auto alongwith driver on the driver seat of such auto/TSR at around 10.00 pm at Jaitpur, Meethapur Road. When he reached nerar Hari Nagar Village one motorcycle/alleged offending vehicle bearing No. DL-3TC-0249 came in very rash and negligent manner and hit the auto from the right side as a result of which such injured/claimant suffered injury in his right leg and such claimant fell down from the auto. That auto driver made him to sit on the side of the road and went away. It is further stated that he do not know the number of such auto/TSR but he can identify such auto driver. But he identified the number of such motorcycle. Thereafter, claimant's family members took him to AIIMS Trauma Center. 3. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 338, IPC filed against the R-1 apart from filing of present DAR. 4. As per record, R-1/ driver cum owner appeared in person and even contested the present case. He filed his reply dated MACT No.: 274/19 Amod Kumar Shah Vs. Vinay Page No. 2 of 29 29.11.2019. In nut sell, it is stated in the reply that R-1 is falsely implicated in the present case. That accident occurred due to zig zag driver of the driver of the TSR. It is further stated that such TRS driver allowed illegal passenger beyond its capacity in the TSR. It is further claimed that injured/petitioner illegally set besides driver's seat and due to such combined effect, injury is suffered by the claimant. That R-1 even tried to help the injured but he stated that injured family member will take him to hospital. As such, it is stated that it is the liability of TSR driver to pay compensation, if any, to the injured. 5. Further, a reply dated 09.05.2019 being filed by the R- 2/insurance company. It is claimed that R-1 breached the terms and condition as he was driving such motorcycle without valid licence. As such, it is submitted that insurance company is not liable to pay the claim at all. It is further stated that it is the case of contributory negligence on the part of injured himself. It is further stated that accident took place due to sole rash and negligent driving of TSR driver including because he made to sit injured besides him on driver seat which is illegal and dangerous. It is further stated that auto driver run away after accident. It is further stated that as such, driver, owner and insurance company if any of such TSR/auto be also added as respondent. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 09.05.2019 by learned Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. 3 . Relief. 7. As per record, injured examined himself only as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the OPD card, MLC and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/9. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-2 and same was adopted by R-1/ driver cum owner. 8. Further, R-1/driver-cum-owner also examined himself. He filed his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit Ex. R-1W-1/B. He was cross-examined by counsel for claimant/petitioner. 9. Further, even insurance company/R-2 examined witness as R-2W-1 Mr. Subham Solanki from his legal department, basically on the aspect of R-1. As per record, despite opportunity given by R-1 or by the petitioner. 10. Arguments in detail were addressed by counsels for petitioner, R-1/driver-cum-owner and R-2/insurance company. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.

It is further stated that unless the right leg of the injured was outside the body of TSR, it is not possible that injury of the present nature is caused to him as a result of collision with the another vehicle/motorcycle in question. It is further argued that as such, injured cannot be given benefit of his own wrong. As such, it is further stated that on the face of record, it is a case of contributory negligence. It is further argued that at least 50% be deducted on account of such contributory negligence. Learned counsel also relied certain case law in this regard. 26.
